name: Qian Ouyang
identity: Machine learning for materials and molecular simulation.
metaDescription: Qian Ouyang, AI undergraduate at Xi'an Jiaotong University and Notre Dame research assistant, interested in molecular simulation and efficient MLIPs.
introduction: I study Artificial Intelligence at Xi'an Jiaotong University and work as a research assistant in Prof. Tengfei Luo's group at the University of Notre Dame. I am interested in how molecular models describe materials, and how to make their simulations more efficient.
biography: I am a fourth-year undergraduate majoring in Artificial Intelligence in the Artificial Intelligence Experimental Class at Xi'an Jiaotong University. I am also a research assistant in Prof. Tengfei Luo's group in the Department of Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering at the University of Notre Dame.

I enrolled at Xi'an Jiaotong University in 2023 and expect to graduate in 2027. I have been a research assistant at Notre Dame since October 2025. I was a visiting student at Notre Dame from August to December 2025 and returned for summer research through iSURE from July to September 2026.

My research interests include JEPA-style representation learning for molecular dynamics and coarse-grained modeling. I am particularly interested in optimizing machine learning interatomic potentials for high-performance computing: understanding computational redundancy, reducing GPU memory requirements, and making molecular simulation more efficient.
